title: agentjail profile
description: Machine-readable description of an agentjail profile. A profile is written as TOML (profiles/<name>.toml) and validated against this document before anything is launched. The document is agent-agnostic: it never names a harness, a session, or a vendor-specific credential. See docs/profiles.md for the prose reference and the semantics of each field.

version.description: Profile format version. Bumped only for breaking changes.

description.description: Human-readable summary of what this jail is for.

mounts.description: Host paths exposed inside the jail. Anything not listed here does not exist inside the jail.

env.description: Literal, non-secret environment values. Names that look like credentials are rejected: use secrets[] instead.

secrets.description: Credentials, by reference only. Inline values are rejected. Secrets are delivered to the agent process environment (or to a tmpfs file) at launch time and never baked into the image or a bind mount.

allOf.description: network.mode=none means no route at all and no resolver: no-egress mode cannot carry destinations, which is a different claim from an allowlist profile that asks for nothing.
network.mode=allowlist requires a DNS strategy that does not hand the agent a general-purpose resolver; an omitted egress list and an explicit empty list are the same grant of nothing.

absolutePath.description: Absolute POSIX path inside the jail (or on the host for mounts).

name.description: Fully qualified image reference including registry and optional tag, e.g. ghcr.io/breinich/agentjail-base:1.

digest.description: Content digest the reference must resolve to. Tags are never trusted on their own.

source.description: Absolute host path. Paths backed by FUSE (AppImage mounts such as /tmp/.mount_*/, gvfs, /run/user/*/doc) are rejected during semantic validation: crun cannot bind-mount them into the jail. Copy the runtime into the image or into a workspace-visible directory instead.

read_only.description: Mount read-only. Defaults to true; writable mounts must be requested explicitly.

required.description: Fail the launch if the host path is missing. When false the mount is skipped and the launch continues.

name.description: Optional label used in diagnostics. Never printed with a value.

source.description: Where the reference points: a host environment variable, a host file, or a credential-store entry.

ref.description: The reference itself: env var name, absolute host file path, or credential-store item identifier. Never the secret value.

delivery.description: How the secret reaches the agent: as an environment variable of the agent process (default) or as a file on a tmpfs-backed path inside the jail.

target.description: Where the secret appears inside the jail: the environment variable name when delivery=env, an absolute path when delivery=file.

mode.description: File mode for delivery=file (default 0400). Not allowed for delivery=env.

allOf.description: delivery=env targets an environment variable name.
delivery=file targets an absolute path inside a tmpfs mount.
mode is only meaningful for file delivery.

name.description: Attach to this existing podman network instead of creating one. The single-route invariant is verified from outside (this network's metadata) and from inside (inside the jail) on every start; run refuses a network that is not internal. Omit to let the launcher create a dedicated internal network.

class.description: Egress class, required with mode="allowlist". Either one this build ships (model, external, internal, resolved from gateway/classes/<class>.toml) or an operator-defined class named by network.class_dir and pinned by network.class_digest. The class is the internal podman network the jail joins; the profile may ask for less than its class permits, never more, and the agent cannot change its network membership from inside the jail.

class_dir.description: Absolute host directory holding <class>.toml for an operator-defined class. Validated with the same rules as a built-in class, bind-mounted read-only into the gateway container, and pinned by network.class_digest. Give both or neither; an operator class may not reuse a built-in class name.

class_digest.description: sha256 of the class file that network.class_dir names, in the same form as image.digest. Required with network.class_dir: a class file that can change under a reviewed profile is not a pin, and a mismatch refuses the run.

mode.description: none: the jail is attached to an internal network with no route out. allowlist: the only route out is the egress gateway, which permits the listed destinations.

dns.description: DNS strategy. Required with no default so it can never be unset by accident: an inherited host search domain can silently resolve internal names and defeat an allowlist. none: no resolver (only with mode="none"). gateway: the class gateway is the resolver and answers only allowlisted names, pinned to loopback. pinned is reserved and refused by validation until it is implemented: the launcher always starts the class gateway as the resolver. With a resolver the launcher additionally passes --dns-search . so host search domains cannot leak in (see docs/threat-model.md).

egress.description: Destinations the egress gateway may permit. An omitted list and an explicit empty array are the same grant of nothing: with mode="allowlist" the jail starts and reaches nothing rather than being refused, and with mode="none" an empty list is the only accepted value.

host.description: DNS name the gateway may resolve and connect to. Wildcards, schemes, paths, and ports belong elsewhere and are rejected.

protocol.description: tls: HTTPS CONNECT with SNI pinned to host. http: plaintext CONNECT. tcp: raw TCP relay to host:port with no protocol inspection.

tmpfs.description: In-jail tmpfs mounts, keyed by absolute path. Every path listed here becomes a size-limited tmpfs; this is how scratch space (including secret delivery paths) gets a hard disk budget.

command.description: Executable to run inside the jail, e.g. pi, claude, codex, opencode, or any other program.

args.description: Default arguments. Supports the placeholders {workdir} and {home}; anything else in braces is rejected.
